unmapped_findings: No Vickers hardness value is reported anywhere in the paper for the hot-rolled 12Al-10Mn-0.4C alloy: the hardness tables (Tables 2, 4, 5, 8 and 9) list only 9Al-10Mn-1C, 12Al-10Mn-1C, 12Al-20Mn-1C, 9Al-20Mn-1C, 9Al-30Mn-1C and 12Al-30Mn1C, so the hot-rolled 12Al-10Mn-0.4C sample has no reported quantitative property.

The 12Al-10Mn-0.4C composition appears in the paper only in the 600 °C heat-treatment context: Fig. 3(a), whose caption prints '2Al-10Mn-0.4C' while the referring text writes '12Al-10Mn-0.4C', and the text stating that at 12% Al the austenite reactions involved the whole volume, with 12Al-10Mn-0.4C precipitation producing a multifaceted microstructure. This 600 °C data belongs to a 600 °C-tempered sibling sample, not to the hot-rolled condition of the present sample.

Hot-rolling at 1150 °C followed by water quenching is the shared as-received (reference) condition applied to all tested Fe–Mn–Al–C alloys, so this sample is a reference-state sample whose specific hardness/microstructure are not individually tabulated in the paper.
The nominal composition of this alloy falls within the composition space defined by Table 1: Al 9–12 wt%, Mn 10–20–30 wt%, C 0.4–1 wt%, Fe balance (this sample: 12 wt% Al, 10 wt% Mn, 0.4 wt% C).
